\section[(ma propre ligne)]{Your own line — the first writing with no model}

\label{lesson:FR-W02-ma-propre-ligne}



\begin{quote}
Everything you have written so far had something to reach for — a shape, a word, a sound.

This does not. You choose the words, from a supply that is closed: only what this book has taught you.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — controlled composition}
Write \textbf{one line} about yourself. Subject, verb, then the rest — the order you already know.

One thing to decide deliberately rather than by accident before you start: \textbf{the accents are letters, not decoration.}

An acute on an \textbf{e} is not a flourish on the same letter; it makes a different sound and, often enough, a different word. A hand that writes French without accents has not written French untidily — it has written something else and hoped the reader would guess.

Write the line. Then read it back and check the accents \textbf{before} you check anything else.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Are French accents decoration? (\textbf{No} — they are part of the letter.)

And what did you choose here that the earlier lessons chose for you? (\textbf{The words.})
\end{tcolorbox}
